cause.flow: Successful workspace switch -> original cache invalidation -> ordinary listener creates a new Map/provider generation and calls router.refresh -> real SWR remounts and reads before full-document navigation.

riskTriage.reason: Deterministic extra work in the exercised authenticated workspace-departure flow; directly reproduced with real React/SWR. No fixed number of real SQL calls is inferred.

findings.result: Only useWorkspaceSwitcher opts into documentNavigation:true, after switchWorkspace returns ok and immediately before the existing awaited clear and location.assign. Existing same-workspace no-op, failed switch, logout, account deletion, connection reset and other callers retain their previous default paths.

invalidate still sets enabled=false, clears the Map, releases hydration and schedules erasure before notifying React. Disabled set() rejects late writes. Existing staleOnFocus.isPaused, useLiveKey.current and prefetchScopedRead guards continue to reject new work for a disabled PersistentReadCache.

The navigation branch retains the old cache reference, marks the existing boundary retired, returns null and lets the connection effect clean up. It creates no fallback Map, increments no generation and issues no router.refresh. The same retired boundary remains retired after parent rerender, ordinary clear and callbacks already queued before disconnect.

The original activeCaches snapshot, per-cache pending queue waits and final IndexedReadStorage.clear remain. The controlled blocked-erasure fixture shows the caller stays pending while memory is already empty and late writes are rejected.

Default options use navigation=false. The normal listener still makes an empty memory provider, increments generation and refreshes. Remote BroadcastChannel messages call invalidate(false), retaining default navigation=false; permission-denied invalidation likewise remains ordinary. Final real React/SWR observations are reads2/refresh1 for all three paths.
The existing global {type:clear} message is preserved. The local retirement boolean is never sent, so another document receives ordinary invalidation rather than a permanent retirement instruction.

No document-global pause flag is introduced. A fresh mounted authorized boundary owns a distinct enabled cache and performs its ordinary first read. The test models this by unmounting/remounting a root; it does not execute a browser or Electron document reload.

Both Native Workspace and Web WorkspaceApp use this shared AuthenticatedReadCache boundary. Server authorization, namespace identity, backend reads, query counters, login/startup windows and checkpoint code are untouched by this patch.
